The Portrait of Henry VIII by Hans Holbein the Younger is one of the most iconic images of the king. In this portrait, Henry VIII is depicted standing with his legs apart, wearing elaborate royal attire. His right hand is resting on the hilt of his sword, and his left hand is holding a single glove. The glove is a symbol of nobility and power, often used in portraits of royalty and nobility during that period.

There is no depiction of Henry VIII holding a turkey leg in this or any well-known portrait. The idea of him holding a turkey leg is not supported by historical or artistic evidence.

Therefore, the correct answer is that King Henry is holding a glove in the Portrait of Henry VIII.
